content: The Founder stands at the window and pushes one packet towards the Plant Specialist with a single finger. 'You agreed with me in the report, no invented germination rate. So what do we actually say to someone whose seed doesn't come up?'
round_time: Late morning, Day 1 - Pain point 1: the dead marigold

content: Head of Product writes three sub-headings under PP1: PREVENT, REMEDY, KNOW. 'Three separate problems. Fewer seeds dying, what we do when one dies, and what we actually know about our seed. Each needs an owner.'
round_time: Late morning, Day 1 - Pain point 1: the dead marigold

content: Research points at the KNOW column. 'The only thing worse than no germination figure is a made-up one. But we can find out. We also have real Archive 001 buyers. Message every one of them: did it sprout, did it bloom, did it die, what did you do? A bloom-or-not follow-up costs nothing but our time.'
round_time: Late morning, Day 1 - Pain point 1: the dead marigold

proposals.text: Bloom-or-not follow-up message to every real Archive 001 buyer (sprouted / bloomed / died / what they did)
proposals.test: response rate and outcome tally from real buyers

content: Brand looks at the empty lid and pictures a laminated instruction sheet with clip-art suns. Their stomach tightens. If there's going to be a guide, they want it to read like part of the archive, not a seed company leaflet.
round_time: Late morning, Day 1 - Pain point 1: the dead marigold

content: The Designer cuts a scrap of card to the inside diameter of the tin lid, then lays it flat. 'Proposal: a printed card that sits inside the lid, so you see it the moment you open it. Front: the number and the story. Back: how to grow it. It adds no hand-painting time. Tin size is UNKNOWN, so I've cut this to these leftovers, not to a spec.'
round_time: Late morning, Day 1 - Pain point 1: the dead marigold

proposals.text: Printed growing card inside the tin lid (front: number and story; back: growing steps)
proposals.test: bloom-or-not tally for Archive 002 buyers who received the card vs Archive 001 buyers who did not

content: The Plant Specialist taps the packet against the sill. 'What we say is: we're testing. I propose sowing a sample from the actual seed lot this week, in conditions written down, and recording what comes up. We publish a germination figure only when it's measured, and we label it as our test, not a promise. Meanwhile the guide covers what we can stand behind: when to sow, how deep, water, light, how long before you'd expect to see anything. Grow method in a tin is still UNKNOWN. I'd test that too, tin versus a pot.'
round_time: Late morning, Day 1 - Pain point 1: the dead marigold

proposals.text: Real germination test on a sample of the actual seed lot (documented conditions); publish only a measured result, labelled as Preserve's own test
proposals.cost: low (seeds, soil, two weeks of time)
proposals.test: the germination test itself; repeated per seed lot

proposals.text: Side test of grow method: sowing in a tin vs a pot (grow method UNKNOWN)

content: Growth stops scrolling. 'Film the test. A time-lapse of our own trays from day one is content. Tell people we're testing our own seed before we sell you another one. That's a hook I can use and nobody here can call it cheap.'
round_time: Late morning, Day 1 - Pain point 1: the dead marigold

proposals.text: Film the germination test as a time-lapse for the funnel

content: Community is already nodding. 'And send the follow-up from a person, not the brand voice. Some of those buyers might have a dead seed sitting on a balcony right now. The first message they get from us shouldn't be a survey.'
round_time: Late morning, Day 1 - Pain point 1: the dead marigold

content: CX writes REMEDY in capitals next to their name. 'I'll write the dead-seed flow. Proposal: buyer tells us it didn't come up, sends a photo, we reply within a set time with a replacement. And the follow-up offers it to Archive 001 buyers retroactively. Those five dead seeds in the sim are the people we lose. Real ones might be sitting in our DMs.'
round_time: Late morning, Day 1 - Pain point 1: the dead marigold

proposals.text: Dead-seed remedy flow: buyer reports non-sprouting with a photo, Preserve replies within a set time with a replacement; offered retroactively to Archive 001 buyers
proposals.cost: depends on seed + shipping cost (UNKNOWN; Finance to model)
proposals.test: number of claims, resolution time, repeat intent of claimants

content: Ops frowns at the packets on the warm windowsill. 'Where were these stored before they went in the tins? Heat, damp, how long in transit? I don't actually know, and the seed might have been fine before we got to it. Put storage in the test.'
round_time: Late morning, Day 1 - Pain point 1: the dead marigold

proposals.text: Record and fix seed storage and packing conditions (cool, dry, dated packets) before Archive 002 packing
proposals.test: include stored-vs-fresh samples in the germination test

content: Finance raises the pen. 'Retroactive replacements for Archive 001: how many buyers, what does a seed packet plus shipping cost? I'm not against it. I just don't sign blank cheques. Get me the two numbers and I'll model it tonight.'
round_time: Late morning, Day 1 - Pain point 1: the dead marigold

content: Legal: 'If you publish your own test result, say how it was done and don't present it as a guarantee. Something like: in our test of this lot, X of Y sprouted. Verify the exact wording with a professional.'
round_time: Late morning, Day 1 - Pain point 1: the dead marigold
